title: orders-service 5xx spike after traffic increase
description: orders-service is returning HTTP 500 and 503 errors for a large share of requests. Latency climbed sharply at the same time as a traffic increase. Requests appear to be waiting on the database.
symptoms: request threads blocked waiting for database connections
error_messages: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections

recent_changes.description: v2.11.0: Copy change on order confirmation page
Flash sale campaign launched; traffic about 2.5x baseline

ground_truth_root_cause: PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion. The traffic surge from the flash sale saturated the fixed pool of 100 connections, slow queries held connections longer, and requests queued until they timed out and returned 5xx.
expected_remediation: Raise the connection pool size within the database max_connections budget, put PgBouncer in front of PostgreSQL, terminate idle-in-transaction sessions, rate limit campaign traffic, and restart the service only if connections have leaked.

title: orders-service pods OOMKilled and restarting
description: Pods for orders-service are being terminated with exit code 137 and restarting. Memory climbs steadily until each container is killed.

recent_changes.description: v2.12.0: Increase in-process product catalog cache from 256MB to 2GB

expected_remediation: Raise the memory limit to 1Gi and cap the cache size through configuration. If that cannot be done quickly, roll back the release that enlarged the cache.

title: Kafka consumer lag growing for analytics-consumer
description: Consumer lag for the analytics-consumer consumer group has grown past 200k messages and throughput has dropped. The group keeps rebalancing.
symptoms: consumer lag above 200k messages and rising
error_messages: consumer poll timeout has expired; leaving group
Attempt to heartbeat failed since group is rebalancing

recent_changes.description: Increased max.poll.records from 500 to 5000

ground_truth_root_cause: The consumer group is stuck in a rebalance loop. Raising max.poll.records to 5000 made each batch take longer than max.poll.interval.ms, so consumers are evicted from the group before they commit offsets.
expected_remediation: Revert max.poll.records to 500 or raise max.poll.interval.ms above the worst batch time, then scale consumers to the partition count to drain the backlog.

title: payments-service 5xx errors after deployment
description: Minutes after a new release of payments-service, roughly a third of requests fail with HTTP 500. No traffic change was observed.
symptoms: HTTP 500 rate jumped from under 1% to about 30%
errors started within minutes of a deployment
stack traces point to the response serializer
error_messages: java.lang.NullPointerException at AddressSerializer.serialize(AddressSerializer.java:48)
GET /api/v1/addresses 500 Internal Server Error

recent_changes.description: v2.13.0: Refactor serializer for address payloads

ground_truth_root_cause: The latest deployment introduced a regression in the address response serializer. Records without an optional field throw a NullPointerException and return 500.
expected_remediation: Roll back to the previous version, then add a regression test for addresses without the optional field before redeploying.

title: DNS lookup failures from api-gateway
description: api-gateway is intermittently failing to resolve internal service names. Calls to downstream services fail with lookup timeouts.
symptoms: errors spread across all downstream dependencies
error_messages: dial tcp: lookup payments-service.commerce.svc.cluster.local on 10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout
getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN orders-service.commerce.svc.cluster.local

recent_changes.description: Node pool rotation reduced CoreDNS replicas from 3 to 1

ground_truth_root_cause: CoreDNS was left with a single replica after a node pool rotation. With ndots:5 search path expansion each lookup produces several queries, and the single replica is overloaded and drops requests.
expected_remediation: Scale CoreDNS back to at least 3 replicas, add a PodDisruptionBudget, enable NodeLocal DNSCache, and lower ndots for services that call external names.

title: TLS handshake failures on api-gateway
description: Clients connecting to api-gateway fail the TLS handshake. Errors started at midnight UTC and affect every client.
symptoms: errors started at a round clock time
error_messages: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate expired
ground_truth_root_cause: The TLS certificate for api-gateway expired because cert-manager could not renew it. The ACME DNS-01 challenge has been failing since the DNS provider credentials were revoked.
expected_remediation: Issue and install a replacement certificate, restore the DNS provider credentials used by cert-manager, and alert on certificates expiring within 21 days.

title: Spike in 401 responses on auth-service
description: auth-service is rejecting valid user sessions with HTTP 401. The failures began shortly after the identity provider rotated its signing key.
symptoms: 401 rate above 40% for logged in users
only tokens issued after the rotation are rejected
users forced to log in repeatedly
error_messages: JWT verification failed: kid 2026-key-b not found in JWKS
401 Unauthorized: invalid token signature

recent_changes.description: Identity provider rotated JWT signing key

ground_truth_root_cause: The identity provider rotated its JWT signing key, but auth-service caches the JWKS for 24 hours and does not refetch when it sees an unknown key id, so tokens signed with the new key are rejected.
expected_remediation: Force a JWKS refresh by restarting or reloading the service, change the verifier to refetch JWKS on unknown kid, and publish new keys before they are used for signing.

title: search-api latency up as Redis evicts keys
description: Redis used by search-api hit maxmemory and is evicting keys. Cache hit ratio collapsed and latency and database load increased.
symptoms: cache hit ratio dropped from 95% to about 40%
error_messages: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'

recent_changes.description: v2.16.0: Store user sessions in the shared cache cluster

ground_truth_root_cause: Redis reached maxmemory because a release started writing session keys without a TTL. The allkeys-lru policy evicts hot cache entries instead, so the hit ratio collapsed and requests fell through to the database.
expected_remediation: Set a TTL on session keys and expire the existing ones, move sessions to a separate Redis instance, and alert on memory above 85% of maxmemory.

title: search-api p99 latency high while CPU looks normal
description: search-api p99 latency has tripled. Average CPU utilization looks moderate, but containers are being throttled heavily.
error_messages: request exceeded latency budget of 500ms

recent_changes.description: Reduced CPU limit from 2 cores to 500m for cost savings

ground_truth_root_cause: The CPU limit was cut to 500m. Request handling is bursty, so containers use their CFS quota early in each period and are throttled, which inflates latency even though average utilization looks moderate.
expected_remediation: Restore the CPU limit to 2 cores or remove the limit while keeping the request, and alert on container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total.

title: analytics-consumer pods evicted due to disk pressure
description: Nodes running analytics-consumer report DiskPressure and the kubelet is evicting pods. Writes fail with no space left on device.
error_messages: write /var/log/app/analytics-consumer.log: no space left on device
The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage

recent_changes.description: Set LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG while investigating a billing bug

ground_truth_root_cause: Debug logging was left enabled after an investigation. The service wrote full request payloads to local log files, filled the node's ephemeral storage and triggered kubelet evictions.
expected_remediation: Set LOG_LEVEL back to INFO, clear the oversized log files, set ephemeral-storage requests and limits, and log to stdout with rotation.

title: shipping-service requests timing out on downstream dependency
description: shipping-service requests are slow and timing out. Threads are blocked waiting on the third party shipping rates provider.
symptoms: request threads blocked on outbound HTTP calls
circuit breaker opening and closing repeatedly
error_messages: Timeout calling shipping-rates-provider after 10000ms
CircuitBreaker 'shipping-rates' is OPEN and does not permit further calls
ground_truth_root_cause: The third party shipping rates provider degraded to over 10 seconds p99. The service had no tight timeout or fallback, so request threads blocked on the provider and latency cascaded to callers.
expected_remediation: Cut the provider timeout to 2 seconds, serve cached rates as a fallback, tune the circuit breaker, and open a ticket with the provider.

title: Latency spike on search-api listing endpoints
description: Listing endpoints on search-api slowed from about 100ms to several seconds after a feature release. Database CPU is high.
symptoms: slow query log full of sequential scans
error_messages: slow query: Seq Scan on products (rows=41234001) took 3120ms

recent_changes.description: v2.17.0: Add region filter to product listing API

ground_truth_root_cause: The new region filter queries products.region, which has no index, so every listing request runs a sequential scan over a 40M row table.
expected_remediation: Create an index on products.region with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, or disable the region filter until the index exists. Add EXPLAIN checks to query reviews.

title: billing-service errors after failed schema migration
description: billing-service is failing requests with missing column errors. The schema migration in the latest release did not complete but the application was rolled out.
symptoms: SQL errors referencing a missing column
migration job exited with a lock timeout
new application version running on all pods
error_messages: ERROR: column "discount_code" does not exist
migration 0042_add_discount_code failed: canceling statement due to lock timeout

recent_changes.description: v2.18.0: Add discount codes to invoices (migration 0042)

ground_truth_root_cause: Schema migration 0042 failed on a lock timeout, but the deploy pipeline did not gate on migration success. The new version expects the discount_code column, which does not exist.
expected_remediation: Roll back the application to the previous version, rerun migration 0042 with a lock_timeout during low traffic, and make the pipeline block rollout when a migration fails.

symptoms: failures started when a flag was changed
error_messages: PricingEngineV2: KeyError 'currency_rounding' for currency EUR

recent_changes.description: Ramped feature flag new-pricing-engine from 5% to 100%

ground_truth_root_cause: Ramping new-pricing-engine to 100% exposed a code path that has no rounding configuration for non-USD currencies, so those requests fail.
expected_remediation: Turn the new-pricing-engine flag off, add the missing currency rounding configuration, and ramp again gradually with error rate guards.

title: api-gateway returning 502 from load balancer
description: The load balancer in front of api-gateway is returning 502 and 503. Pods are running and healthy from inside the cluster.
symptoms: target group reports no healthy targets
error_messages: 502 Bad Gateway
Target group api-gateway-tg has no healthy targets

recent_changes.description: Terraform change updated target group health check path to /healthz

ground_truth_root_cause: A Terraform change set the target group health check path to /healthz, but the service serves /health. Every target fails its health check and the load balancer has nothing to route to.
expected_remediation: Revert the health check path to /health through Terraform and add a plan check that validates health check paths against the service.

title: payments-service cannot authenticate to database after credential rotation
description: New database connections from payments-service fail with password authentication errors. Existing connections still work.
symptoms: errors started right after a scheduled credential rotation
error_messages: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "payments-service_app"

recent_changes.description: Automated rotation of database credentials in Secrets Manager

ground_truth_root_cause: Secrets Manager rotated the database password, but payments-service reads credentials only at startup. New connections still use the old password and fail.
expected_remediation: Do a rolling restart of payments-service so it loads the new secret, then add secret reloading or a dual-credential rotation strategy.

title: notification-worker getting AccessDenied from AWS
description: notification-worker is failing to write to S3 with AccessDenied after an IAM change was applied.
symptoms: failures started after an IAM Terraform apply
error_messages: AccessDenied: assumed-role/notification-worker-role is not authorized to perform: s3:PutObject

recent_changes.description: Terraform refactor consolidated IAM policies for data services

ground_truth_root_cause: An IAM Terraform refactor dropped the s3:PutObject statement from the notification-worker role, so every upload is denied.
expected_remediation: Restore the s3:PutObject statement on the role, reapply Terraform, and add policy tests or IAM Access Analyzer checks to the pipeline.

title: Queue backlog growing for notification-worker
description: The SQS queue consumed by notification-worker has grown past 150k messages. Workers are running but throughput is near zero.
symptoms: the same message id failing repeatedly
error_messages: Failed to process message: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1
ground_truth_root_cause: A malformed poison message fails processing and is redelivered forever. The queue has no dead letter queue, so it blocks the workers and the backlog grows.
expected_remediation: Move the poison message aside, configure a dead letter queue with maxReceiveCount of 5, and make the worker skip unparseable payloads.

title: inventory-service in CrashLoopBackOff after config change
description: All new inventory-service pods exit within seconds of starting and are in CrashLoopBackOff. Old pods are still serving.
symptoms: container exits with code 1 within 3 seconds
only pods started after a config change are affected
error_messages: panic: missing required environment variable DATABASE_URL
Back-off restarting failed container

recent_changes.description: ConfigMap cleanup renamed DATABASE_URL to DB_CONNECTION_URL

ground_truth_root_cause: A ConfigMap cleanup renamed DATABASE_URL to DB_CONNECTION_URL. The service requires DATABASE_URL, so new containers panic on startup and crash loop.
expected_remediation: Restore the DATABASE_URL key in the ConfigMap and restart the rollout, then validate required keys in CI.

title: checkout-api saturated during peak traffic, HPA not scaling
description: During the daily traffic peak checkout-api CPU is saturated and latency is high. The HorizontalPodAutoscaler is pinned at its maximum replica count.
error_messages: HPA checkout-api: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 4

recent_changes.description: HPA maxReplicas lowered from 20 to 4

ground_truth_root_cause: HPA maxReplicas was lowered from 20 to 4, so checkout-api could not scale out for peak traffic. Pods saturate on CPU and latency climbs.
expected_remediation: Restore maxReplicas to 20, and alert when an HPA sits at maxReplicas for more than 10 minutes.

title: checkout-api 5xx spike after traffic increase
description: checkout-api is returning HTTP 500 and 503 errors for a large share of requests. Latency climbed sharply at the same time as a traffic increase. Requests appear to be waiting on the database.
symptoms: request threads blocked waiting for database connections
error_messages: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections

recent_changes.description: v2.25.0: Copy change on order confirmation page
Flash sale campaign launched; traffic about 2.5x baseline

ground_truth_root_cause: PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion. The traffic surge from the flash sale saturated the fixed pool of 100 connections, slow queries held connections longer, and requests queued until they timed out and returned 5xx.
expected_remediation: Raise the connection pool size within the database max_connections budget, put PgBouncer in front of PostgreSQL, terminate idle-in-transaction sessions, rate limit campaign traffic, and restart the service only if connections have leaked.
